what: whether a retrieval strategy selected on one task family (half the topics, lexically hard queries) transfers to held-out topics and to the lexically easy condition

config.dataSeedPerRun: the seed itself, so each seed is an independent corpus

encoder.note: the pipeline's own serving configuration; not tuned for this experiment

protocol.lessonRule: mean delta >= 0.01 and every seed the same direction
protocol.transferRule: transferred needs mean delta >= 0.01, no seed against, and >= 3 seeds up

development.rule: mean delta >= 0.01 on mrr and the same direction in every seed

notes: the best strategy on the development family is the baseline 'equal-trust' itself, so the paired deltas below are zero by construction. The evidence in this run is the per-strategy comparison against that baseline on each family, not the subject line.

no candidate beat the a-priori baseline 'equal-trust' under the registered rule, so there was no lesson to transfer. The target families below are still measured and reported as observations, without a transfer claim.

the development winner 'equal-trust' is not the winner on held-out-low ('coverage-weighted' is). No transfer claim is made here: nothing cleared the development bar, so this says the best strategy is family-dependent, nothing more.

the development winner 'equal-trust' is not the winner on held-out-high ('coverage-weighted' is). No transfer claim is made here: nothing cleared the development bar, so this says the best strategy is family-dependent, nothing more.
